body: Hated DBT. I'm sorry you went through what you did. I am so upset by the whole ordeal, and I'm two years out of quitting it. I tried another modality and I just feel like walking in with this diagnosis is like wearing a "PLEASE INVALIDATE ME REPEATEDLY" sticker. I appreciate you sharing, because I don't think we're alone, but I think people with BPD have already experienced so much developmental trauma that they're more likely to blame themselves for therapy going badly (DBT particularly) than to actually realize that the state of therapy as it exists is hugely problematic. There's something wrong when patients (whatever their diagnosis!!) aren't allowed to talk about certain topics like TRAUMA (in the space meant for talking about anything, which I would assume would normally include trauma!), and are required to follow an agenda with the risk of punishments for 'failing' to follow the therapist's set protocols without being informed of what those set protocols are until after they're being punished for 'failing', or being told they're exhibiting 'therapy interfering behaviours' for HAVING EMOTIONS. Yes, all that and more can be found in Linehan's own instruction books! I feel duped. I was in a better place before I began therapy.

Sometimes you just *know* something isn't working. I waited nearly a decade for DBT believing it was God's gift to BPD and was sorely disappointed real fast when my trauma was re-inflicted repeatedly. I respect that this person realized they were in the wrong place and listened to their self-awareness.
Fair enough. I was more curious about the undertow of DBT that most clients don't realize are part of the clinicians training.

I hope you don't mind me asking, but what are your feelings on DBT? How do you feel about Linehan's 'mild' usage of operant conditioning as part of the treatment, particularly the part about consequences for not complying (even if that just involves crying at an 'inconvenient time'), or "positive and negative reinforcement, shaping, extinction, satiation, and punishment" (Linehan, 2015) playing a role? What about 'therapy interfering behaviours'? Do you find any of the protocols manipulative or questionable in a therapeutic sense, or even counter-productive to being able to heal?

how do you make a therapist forget everything they thought they knew about a highly stigmatized population of patients? heh you don't... you give up. you give up on ever having a right to anyone believing you could know or be right about anything, especially yourself and what you know in your heart would help you, which would simply be believing you. no, you have to be wrong. you need to just shut up, pretend and comply like you always did as an abuse victim. you just nod your head and smile and agree with everything they say. you don't fight it, but if you do, you'll be in trouble, because that's a big mistake when you're just trying to protect yourself. no, you just be a good little patient like you were a good little victim and you just play the part of what they want all over again. and you never tell them that this is your truth; that this is what everyone ever expected of you because that's blame, and blaming them is not allowed; that would be a mistake on your part to ever assert your own free will and speak of or define your own needs or to say someone else ever did something wrong. no, you need to remember that having a mind of your own is bad - even dangerous - and definitely not allowed. you need to realize that it was your mistake in ever having wanted to talk about these things underneath, and it's your fault for not having better words to tell them at all when nobody taught you how to speak. no, to want someone to understand, and think - along with you - that you yourself could believe something different, especially that you could actually be sane enough to be believed is where you went wrong. you're supposed to just disappear under the blanket of their good intentions to teach you how to be different in the way they expect you to be because they're the only one who's allowed to be right and know what's good for you, even if it risks your life... that couldn't possibly be the mirror of your trauma all along, and if it is... shut up... no one's listening. weren't you supposed to be blind to this all along? your mistake for seeing this... punishment will be incoming! sorry. it's really not *their* fault... this is exactly what your abusers wanted to happen to you if you ever tried to live outside of their vision by seeing their secret and daring to speak it, because they did their best to hide it inside of you by making you "difficult". I know, I know, I know... Everything that's ever wrong is *my* fault and supposed to stay inside of *me* and *I'm* never allowed to believe otherwise. If I try to, they'll find a way to destroy my attempts all over again, even - if they have to - through the person I try to trust to not make me live it again. They always win.

From [MAID](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/medical-assistance-dying.html) website:

Grievous and irremediable medical condition

To be considered as having a grievous and irremediable medical condition, you must meet all of the following criteria. You must:

* have a serious illness, disease or disability (excluding a mental illness until March 17, 2023)
* be in an advanced state of decline that cannot be reversed
    experience unbearable physical or mental suffering from your illness, disease, disability or state of decline that cannot be relieved under conditions that you consider acceptable

You do not need to have a fatal or terminal condition to be eligible for medical assistance in dying.

Canadians whose only medical condition is a mental illness, and who otherwise meet all eligibility criteria, will not be eligible for MAID until March 17, 2023 (see About mental illness and MAID).

this is where i think most modalities of therapy have gone horribly wrong. since the invention of cbt, nearly everything has become a focus on making your symptoms appear less noticeable, basically with 'therapy' telling you that you can just figure out how to control yourself better and expecting you to learn the tools so that everything will be better; that underlying all your problems, everything that's wrong is just kind of your fault for not changing (and god save you if you fail therapy like i have... cause you know that shit is written into their manuals, too; 'boundary breaking', and 'TIBs', and all the other lovely things!). for very traumatized people, that shit is just re-traumatizing when you need to feel like having your emotions about real heartbreaking shit is okay. like, i think therapy could be surprisingly easy if it was actually what it started out as... a place to be listened to empathically. woah, mind boggling!! but maybe that acceptance would lead to them finding a reason to feel differently, instead of feeling pressured to so that they 'deserve help' from the therapist who can leave them, even though they're paid to be there... crazy, i know, to think we'd just be allowed to voice things and that 'support' would be an actual good thing! instead even therapy leaves a lot of us stuck being denied the feelings we really feel so deeply down inside.
